area: E — permissions, privileges and scoping across all three new features

cases.title: Setting a customer's payment terms follows CUSTOMER_MANAGE for every seeded role
cases.steps: Created one user per seeded role (prefix 'e'); each called PUT /api/customers/{custT} with a different paymentTerm, re-read as admin after each call.
cases.expected: 200 and the term stored for ADMIN, CASHIER, CUSTOMER_SUCCESS_POC (the roles holding CUSTOMER_MANAGE); 403 and the stored term unchanged for VIEWER, CUSTOMER, SALES_POC, COLLECTION_POC.
cases.actual: Exactly that. ADMIN 200 (NET_15 stored), CASHIER 200 (NET_30), CUSTOMER_SUCCESS_POC 200 (NET_60); VIEWER/CUSTOMER/SALES_POC/COLLECTION_POC 403 'You do not have permission for this action' with the previous term still stored.

cases.title: Invoice creation follows INVOICE_MANAGE, and the due date defaults from the customer's terms for every role that can create one
cases.steps: Each role POSTed /api/invoices for custA (paymentTerm NET_45) with invoiceDate = today 00:00Z.
cases.expected: 200 for ADMIN, CASHIER, SALES_POC (INVOICE_MANAGE holders) with dueDate = invoiceDate + 45 and paymentTerm NET_45; 403 for VIEWER, CUSTOMER, CUSTOMER_SUCCESS_POC, COLLECTION_POC.
cases.actual: ADMIN/CASHIER/SALES_POC 200, dueDate 2026-11-04 = 2026-09-20 + 45, paymentTerm NET_45 in all three. VIEWER/CUSTOMER/CUSTOMER_SUCCESS_POC/COLLECTION_POC 403. No role gets a different default.

cases.title: Overriding a due date needs INVOICE_MANAGE and nothing narrower (impl doc §1 answer 2)
cases.steps: One fresh invoice per role on custA, then PATCH /api/invoices/{id} {paymentTerm:CUSTOM, dueDate: today+99}; re-read as admin.
cases.expected: 200 with the date stored and paymentTerm CUSTOM for INVOICE_MANAGE holders; 403 with the date unmoved for everyone else. No separate override privilege.
cases.actual: ADMIN/CASHIER/SALES_POC 200, stored 2026-12-28 with term CUSTOM. VIEWER/CUSTOMER/CUSTOMER_SUCCESS_POC/COLLECTION_POC 403 with the invoice still at 2026-11-04 / NET_45.

cases.title: GET /api/dashboard/outstanding-by-age needs INVOICE_VIEW; every role that holds it gets the new bucket labels
cases.steps: All seven roles called the endpoint, plus a purpose-built role holding only EXPORT_DATA.
cases.expected: 200 for all seven seeded roles (all hold INVOICE_VIEW); 403 without INVOICE_VIEW; buckets Not yet due / 1–30 / 31–60 / 61–90 / Over 90.
cases.actual: 200 for all seven, with exactly those five labels in that order for every role. The EXPORT_DATA-only role got 403.

cases.title: Ageing Coverage is unchanged in meaning per role: ALL / BOOK / OWN
cases.steps: Read the coverage field returned to each role.
cases.expected: OWN for a self-service customer; BOOK for a POC without SCOPE_OVERRIDE; ALL for anyone with SCOPE_OVERRIDE.
cases.actual: ADMIN ALL, CASHIER ALL, VIEWER ALL, CUSTOMER OWN, SALES_POC BOOK, CUSTOMER_SUCCESS_POC ALL, COLLECTION_POC ALL — which matches the SCOPE_OVERRIDE grants in DataSeeder (only SALES_POC lacks it).

cases.title: The buckets a scoped caller gets add up to exactly the open balance that caller can list
cases.steps: For SALES_POC (BOOK) and the self-service CUSTOMER (OWN): summed the bucket amounts and counts, then summed balance over GET /api/invoices (their own scope) excluding CANCELLED and zero-balance rows.
cases.expected: Bucket total == visible open balance, bucket count == visible open count; no money from outside the caller's scope leaks into the chart.
cases.actual: SALES_POC: buckets 1185.00 / 12 vs visible open 1185.00 / 12. CUSTOMER: buckets 1185.00 / 12 vs visible open 1185.00 / 12. Both reconcile exactly; both list pages covered the whole set (13 rows <= page size 50).

cases.title: filter=overdue:eq:true honours the existing scope rules for every role
cases.steps: GET /api/invoices?filter=overdue:eq:true&size=50 as each role, and again narrowed to custA.
cases.expected: 200 for all seven; every returned row has overdue=true; a self-service customer sees only its own; a POC without SCOPE_OVERRIDE sees only its book and gets a locked chip.
cases.actual: 200 for all seven; every row overdue=true in every response. ADMIN/CASHIER/VIEWER/CUSTOMER_SUCCESS_POC/COLLECTION_POC saw the full set (6 in that pass, lockedFilters []). CUSTOMER saw 1 (its own). SALES_POC saw 1 with lockedFilters ['salesPocUserId:eq:59'] while ADMIN saw 24 on the same call in a later pass.

cases.title: Upload needs DOCUMENT_MANAGE plus the parent record's manage privilege, per role and per record kind
cases.steps: Every role POSTed a PDF to /api/documents for custA (CUSTOMER), invA (INVOICE) and payA (PAYMENT).
cases.expected: 201 only where the role holds DOCUMENT_MANAGE and that record kind's manage privilege (customer logins: the record's view privilege instead, per impl doc §4.5).
cases.actual: ADMIN and CASHIER 201 on all three. VIEWER 403 on all three (no DOCUMENT_MANAGE). SALES_POC 201 on INVOICE, 403 on CUSTOMER, 404 on PAYMENT. CUSTOMER_SUCCESS_POC 201 on CUSTOMER, 403 on INVOICE and PAYMENT. COLLECTION_POC 201 on PAYMENT, 403 on CUSTOMER and INVOICE. Self-service CUSTOMER 201 on all three of its own records.

cases.title: List and count need DOCUMENT_VIEW plus the parent record's view privilege
cases.steps: GET /api/documents and /api/documents/count for each role on custA / invA / payA.
cases.expected: 200 wherever the role holds DOCUMENT_VIEW and the record's view privilege and the record is in scope; otherwise 403 or the record's own answer.
cases.actual: 200 for every seeded role on every record kind, except SALES_POC on PAYMENT which is 404 (its payments book is empty). A purpose-built role with DOCUMENT_VIEW but no INVOICE_VIEW got 403, and one with INVOICE_VIEW but no DOCUMENT_VIEW also got 403.

cases.title: Download is authorized on every request and carries the AC-C13 headers
cases.steps: Each role downloaded an admin-uploaded INTERNAL document on custA / invA / payA, plus a SHARED one; inspected response headers.
cases.expected: 200 for DOCUMENT_VIEW + record view + scope; headers Content-Disposition attachment, Content-Type application/octet-stream, X-Content-Type-Options nosniff.
cases.actual: 200 for ADMIN, CASHIER, VIEWER, SALES_POC (customer+invoice), CUSTOMER_SUCCESS_POC, COLLECTION_POC. Headers on every 200: 'attachment; filename="e-invA-internal.pdf"; filename*=UTF-8''e-invA-internal.pdf', application/octet-stream, nosniff. SALES_POC 404 on the payment document; self-service CUSTOMER 404 on INTERNAL and 200 on SHARED.

cases.title: PATCH (description / visibility) needs DOCUMENT_MANAGE plus the record's manage privilege, and is never open to a customer login
cases.steps: Each role PATCHed its own upload where it had one, otherwise an admin-uploaded document on the same record.
cases.expected: 200 only for DOCUMENT_MANAGE + record manage; 403 for a customer login even on its own upload.
cases.actual: Matches the upload matrix exactly (ADMIN/CASHIER all three; SALES_POC invoice only; CUSTOMER_SUCCESS_POC customer only; COLLECTION_POC payment only; VIEWER 403 everywhere). Self-service CUSTOMER 403 on its own upload and 403 on an admin's SHARED document.

cases.title: DELETE needs DOCUMENT_MANAGE, then the record's manage privilege or being the uploader, and is never open to a customer login
cases.steps: Each role deleted its own upload where it had one, otherwise an admin-uploaded document on the same record.
cases.expected: 204 for DOCUMENT_MANAGE + record manage (or uploader); 403 otherwise; 403 for a customer login even on its own upload.
cases.actual: 204 for ADMIN/CASHIER on all three, SALES_POC on invoice, CUSTOMER_SUCCESS_POC on customer, COLLECTION_POC on payment. 403 for VIEWER everywhere, for each POC on the record kinds it cannot manage, and for the self-service CUSTOMER on its own upload. SALES_POC got 404 on the payment document (record out of book).

cases.title: The uploader stands in for the record's manage privilege on DELETE only — not on PATCH, and not for the document privilege
cases.steps: Purpose-built role with DOCUMENT_VIEW+DOCUMENT_MANAGE+INVOICE_VIEW+INVOICE_MANAGE uploaded two documents to invA; INVOICE_MANAGE was then revoked from that role and the same token used again; finally DOCUMENT_MANAGE was revoked too.
cases.expected: After losing INVOICE_MANAGE: upload 403, PATCH 403, DELETE of its own 204, DELETE of somebody else's 403. After losing DOCUMENT_MANAGE: upload/PATCH/DELETE all 403 even on its own, reads still fine.
cases.actual: Exactly that — upload 403, patchOwn 403, deleteOwn 204, deleteSomebodyElses 403; then upload 403, deleteOwn 403, patchOwn 403, list 200, download 200. Privileges are re-read per request, so the revocation took effect on the very next call.

cases.title: canEdit / canDelete on DocumentDto agree with what the API then allows
cases.steps: Compared the flags on listed rows with the status of the matching PATCH/DELETE for every role, including the uploader-without-record-manage case.
cases.expected: No flag that would predictably 403.
cases.actual: ADMIN/CASHIER true/true on all three record kinds; VIEWER false/false; self-service CUSTOMER false/false even on its own upload; each POC true only on the record kind it can manage. In the narrowed-role case canDelete was true only on the row that role had uploaded (id 55) and false on the four others, and the DELETEs answered 204 / 403 to match.

cases.title: A self-service customer sees only SHARED documents on its own records, in list and in count
cases.steps: custA carries an admin-uploaded INTERNAL and an admin-uploaded SHARED document; the customer login listed and counted documents on its customer record, invoice and payment.
cases.expected: Only SHARED rows; count filtered the same way.
cases.actual: Every listed row was SHARED (visibilities ['SHARED'] on all three record kinds); count returned 2 / 2 / 1, matching the SHARED rows only, while staff saw 3 / 3 / 2.

cases.title: A self-service customer cannot download an INTERNAL document on its own record
cases.steps: GET /api/documents/{id}/download as the customer login, for an INTERNAL and for a SHARED document on its own customer record.
cases.expected: 404 for INTERNAL (it does not exist as far as that caller is concerned), 200 for SHARED.
cases.actual: 404 for INTERNAL on all three record kinds, 200 for SHARED. Re-confirmed on a second run.

cases.title: A customer login may upload on its own records and the upload is forced SHARED — PRD deviation recorded in the implementation doc
cases.steps: Customer login POSTed a PDF to its own customer record, invoice and payment, with and without a visibility parameter.
cases.expected: PRD AC-C12 says a customer cannot upload 'unless the Open Questions resolve otherwise'; PRD open question 4 is exactly that, and impl doc §1 answer 4 plus §4.5 record the user's decision to allow it with visibility forced to SHARED. So: 201 with visibility SHARED.
cases.actual: 201 on all three record kinds, visibility SHARED every time including when INTERNAL was asked for; the row is attributed to the customer user. Recorded as a documented deviation, not a defect, per TESTER-RULES ('the PRD wins unless the implementation doc explicitly records a decision to differ').

cases.title: The invoice CSV export requires EXPORT_DATA and INVOICE_VIEW together
cases.steps: POST /api/invoices/export as: a purpose-built role holding only EXPORT_DATA; VIEWER (INVOICE_VIEW, no EXPORT_DATA); CASHIER (both).
cases.expected: 403 when either half is missing, 200 when both are present.
cases.actual: EXPORT_DATA without INVOICE_VIEW 403; INVOICE_VIEW without EXPORT_DATA 403; both present 200. Of the seeded roles, VIEWER and CUSTOMER are 403 and the other five are 200.
cases.evidence: scripts/area-e/out/extra.json -> conjunction.exportDataWithoutInvoiceView / invoiceViewWithoutExportData / bothPresent; out/probe.json -> probes.*.export

cases.title: The exported CSV carries the due date and the overdue flag for every role that may export
cases.steps: Exported invA plus an overdue invoice as each authorised role and read the header row and the values.
cases.expected: Header gains 'Due date' and 'Overdue'; the Sales POC column only where POC identity may be seen.
cases.actual: Header for ADMIN, CASHIER, SALES_POC, CUSTOMER_SUCCESS_POC, COLLECTION_POC: 'Invoice #,Customer,Date,Due date,Total,Paid,Balance,Status,Overdue,Sales POC'. Two data rows each. Export is also scope-checked: SALES_POC exporting a foreign invoice id got 200 with 0 rows rather than that invoice's data.

cases.title: Escalation: document privileges alone reach nothing without the parent record's privilege
cases.steps: Purpose-built role with DOCUMENT_VIEW + DOCUMENT_MANAGE + SCOPE_OVERRIDE and no CUSTOMER/INVOICE/PAYMENT privilege at all; called list, count, download, upload, PATCH, DELETE against invA.
cases.expected: 403 on every one of them.
cases.actual: 403 on list, count, download, upload, PATCH, DELETE — and 403 on GET /api/invoices/{id} itself. Holding the document privileges buys nothing on its own.

cases.title: Escalation: the record's privilege alone reaches no document without DOCUMENT_VIEW
cases.steps: Purpose-built role with INVOICE_VIEW + SCOPE_OVERRIDE and no document privilege; called the same six endpoints against invA.
cases.expected: 403 on every document endpoint, 200 on the invoice itself.
cases.actual: list 403, count 403, download 403, upload 403, PATCH 403, DELETE 403; GET /api/invoices/{id} 200. Both halves of AC-C10's conjunction are genuinely required.

cases.title: Escalation: a role without DOCUMENT_MANAGE calling upload and delete directly is refused
cases.steps: VIEWER (DOCUMENT_VIEW only) POSTed to /api/documents for custA and invA and DELETEd an admin-uploaded document; a role with neither document privilege did the same.
cases.expected: 403, and no document row created.
cases.actual: VIEWER upload 403 on both record kinds with no id returned, delete 403. The role with neither privilege got 403 on upload, list and download. Nothing was created.

cases.title: Escalation: a customer login is refused on every staff-only document endpoint
cases.steps: Customer login called PATCH and DELETE on a document it uploaded itself, and PATCH on an admin-uploaded SHARED document on its own record.
cases.expected: 403 in all three cases (impl doc §4.2: 'never a customer login (403)').
cases.actual: PATCH own 403, DELETE own 403, PATCH admin's SHARED document 403 — the visibility of its own upload could not be flipped to INTERNAL either.

cases.title: A customer login cannot reach another customer's documents by direct id
cases.steps: Customer login on custA requested: list of custB's and invB's documents, download of a known custB document id and a known invB document id, upload to invB, and GET /api/invoices/{invB}.
cases.expected: The document call answers exactly as the record would — 403 for a customer login reaching across.
cases.actual: All six 403. The document answer (403) is identical to the record's own answer (403).

cases.title: A POC cannot reach a record outside their book by direct document id
cases.steps: SALES_POC (no SCOPE_OVERRIDE) requested invB's document list and count, downloaded a known invB document id, uploaded to invB, deleted an invB document, listed custB's documents, and downloaded a payment document on its own customer.
cases.expected: 404 — the same answer the record itself gives a POC outside their book.
cases.actual: GET /api/invoices/{invB} 404 'Invoice not found'; document list 404 'Invoice not found'; count 404; download 404; upload 404; delete 404; custB document list 404; payment document download 404. The foreign document id leaks nothing.

cases.title: SALES_POC's empty payments book closes payment documents entirely
cases.steps: SALES_POC called list / count / download / upload / delete for documents on payA — a payment on a customer that IS in its book, but whose Collection POC is somebody else.
cases.expected: The same answer GET /api/payments/{id} gives: 404, because a caller who is not COLLECTION-assignable and lacks SCOPE_OVERRIDE has an empty payments book, not an unrestricted one.
cases.actual: list 404, count 404, download 404, upload 404, delete 404 — consistent with ScopeResolver.build's nothing() branch. Worth knowing when reading the implementation doc's 'POC ✓ manage' row.

cases.title: An unknown or soft-deleted document id answers 404, never 500
cases.steps: Admin downloaded document id 99999999; then uploaded a document, deleted it, and tried download and PATCH on it.
cases.expected: 404 in every case, with the app's error shape.
cases.actual: Unknown id download 404; deleted document download 404; deleted document PATCH 404. No 500 anywhere.

cases.title: An expired token gets 401, not 500, on reads and on writes
cases.steps: rt.mintToken(user, -60) — a correctly signed token that expired a minute ago — against /api/documents, /api/invoices, /api/dashboard/outstanding-by-age, a document download, and a multipart upload. A live minted token for the same user was used as the control.
cases.expected: 401 on all of them; the control 200.
cases.actual: 401 on all four GETs and 401 on the multipart upload. The live minted token returned 200 on all four, so the tokens themselves are otherwise valid.

cases.title: A malformed, wrongly-signed, unknown-user or absent token gets 401, not 500
cases.steps: Four bad-token shapes ('not-a-jwt'; a valid token with its signature replaced; a correctly signed token for a username that does not exist; no Authorization header) against the same four endpoints, plus 'a.b.c' on POST /api/invoices/export and a garbage token on a multipart upload.
cases.expected: 401 everywhere, no 500, no stack trace.
cases.actual: 401 on all 24 GET combinations, 401 on the malformed multipart upload and 401 on the malformed export POST. No 500 observed.
cases.evidence: scripts/area-e/out/security.json -> auth.malformed / wrongSignature / unknownUser / noToken / malformedUpload / malformedExport

cases.title: DOCUMENT_VIEW and DOCUMENT_MANAGE are seeded idempotently — re-running duplicates nothing and drops nothing
cases.steps: Read DataSeeder.run and its three helpers, then checked the live database through GET /api/privileges and GET /api/roles.
cases.expected: One privilege row per name on any number of boots; no role gaining a duplicate entry; no grant silently dropped.
cases.actual: Privilege rows are created through findByName().orElseGet(save) (DataSeeder:57-63), so a re-run finds each of DOCUMENT_VIEW / DOCUMENT_MANAGE and creates nothing — observed exactly one row for each. Built-in roles go through upsertRole, which assigns a Set (DataSeeder:187-193) — re-running rewrites the same set, so no duplicates and no loss for ADMIN/CASHIER/VIEWER. POC roles go through createRoleIfAbsent (DataSeeder:200-217), which on a second boot adds only privileges in createdNow (empty on a re-run) and skips any the role already holds — so nothing is added twice and nothing is removed. DOCUMENT_MANAGE on CUSTOMER goes through keptOrNew (DataSeeder:108, 225-234): on a re-run createdNow is empty and the privilege is kept because the role already holds it, so the grant survives; an operator's revocation would also survive, which is the stated intent (impl doc §4.5). Observed live: exactly one DOCUMENT_VIEW row and one DOCUMENT_MANAGE row, no duplicate entry in any of the 7 seeded roles' privilege lists, and grants matching the code exactly.

cases.title: The privileges the seven seeded roles actually hold match DataSeeder exactly
cases.steps: GET /api/roles as admin and compared each role's privilege list with DataSeeder.java:65-157.
cases.expected: Byte-for-byte agreement, with DOCUMENT_VIEW on all seven and DOCUMENT_MANAGE on all but VIEWER.
cases.actual: ADMIN 31 privileges (all of Privileges.ALL), CASHIER 17, VIEWER 10, CUSTOMER 12, SALES_POC 17, CUSTOMER_SUCCESS_POC 18, COLLECTION_POC 19 — each exactly the coded set. DOCUMENT_VIEW on all seven; DOCUMENT_MANAGE on all but VIEWER (including CUSTOMER, which got it on the boot that created the privilege).

cases.title: CASHIER retains everything it could do before this feature (PRD §8)
cases.steps: Compared CASHIER's seeded privileges at git HEAD (pre-feature DataSeeder) with the live role, then exercised the pre-feature capabilities end to end as a CASHIER-role user.
cases.expected: The pre-feature set is a subset of the current one, and every pre-feature capability still answers 2xx.
cases.actual: Pre-feature set (CUSTOMER_VIEW/MANAGE, PRODUCT_VIEW, INVOICE_VIEW/MANAGE, PAYMENT_VIEW/MANAGE, NOTIFICATION_VIEW, POC_VIEW, POC_ASSIGN, PROMISE_VIEW, SCOPE_OVERRIDE, EXPORT_DATA) is a strict subset of the live 17; the additions are EMAIL_VIEW, EMAIL_SEND, DOCUMENT_VIEW, DOCUMENT_MANAGE. Exercised live: create customer 200, update customer 200, list products 200, create invoice 200, cancel invoice 200, create payment 200, list payments 200, notifications 200, dashboard billed-by-month 200, dashboard ageing 200, promises list 200, assign a POC 200, export invoices 200, export customers 200, reach an out-of-book invoice via SCOPE_OVERRIDE 200. Nothing regressed.

cases.title: The implementation doc's matrix claims POC roles have document Manage, but each POC can only manage the one record kind its role can manage
cases.steps: Compared line 266 of docs/implementation/invoice-due-dates-and-documents.md with the observed upload/PATCH/DELETE answers for the three POC roles on a customer, an invoice and a payment.
cases.expected: Doc line 266: '| SALES / CUSTOMER_SUCCESS / COLLECTION POC | ✓ | ✓ | inside their POC book (`ScopeResolver`) |' — read literally, all three POC roles can manage documents.
cases.actual: Manage is only ever available on the record kind whose manage privilege the role holds. SALES_POC: upload/PATCH/DELETE 201/200/204 on an INVOICE, 403/403/403 on a CUSTOMER (no CUSTOMER_MANAGE), 404 on a PAYMENT (empty payments book). CUSTOMER_SUCCESS_POC: 201/200/204 on a CUSTOMER, 403 on an INVOICE (no INVOICE_MANAGE) and 403 on a PAYMENT. COLLECTION_POC: 201/200/204 on a PAYMENT, 403 on a CUSTOMER and 403 on an INVOICE. The code is right — this is AC-C10 working — but the matrix PRD §8 asks for is wrong, so a reader planning a role change is misled about two thirds of each POC's document capability.

cases.title: The implementation doc says POC document access is limited to 'their POC book'; two of the three POC roles are not book-limited at all
cases.steps: custB / invB / payB carry no POC seat and no ownership for the three probe POC users (verified through GET /api/customers/{custB}/pocs and the records' own POC fields). Each POC role then listed, downloaded and uploaded documents on those foreign records.
cases.expected: Doc line 266 says POC document access is 'inside their POC book (`ScopeResolver`)'.
cases.actual: Only SALES_POC is book-limited: 404 on GET /api/customers/{custB}, /api/invoices/{invB} and /api/payments/{payB}, 404 on the document list and download for all three, and 404 on uploading to invB (on custB and payB the upload is 403 instead, because the missing CUSTOMER_MANAGE/PAYMENT_MANAGE is refused before scope is reached). CUSTOMER_SUCCESS_POC and COLLECTION_POC both got 200 on GET /api/customers/{custB}, /api/invoices/{invB} and /api/payments/{payB}, 200 on the document list and 200 on downloading an INTERNAL document on each of those foreign records — and CUSTOMER_SUCCESS_POC uploaded to custB (201, then deleted it 204), COLLECTION_POC uploaded to payB (201, 204). Reproduced identically on a second run. Cause: both roles are seeded with SCOPE_OVERRIDE (DataSeeder.java:138 and :153), which by design lifts the book restriction; their ageing Coverage is correspondingly ALL, not BOOK. This is pre-existing, intended role design and NOT an authorization bypass introduced by this feature — the defect is that the matrix PRD §8 asks for describes the opposite, which is exactly the kind of claim an operator would rely on when deciding who to put in a POC role.

cases.title: The implementation doc carries no role × capability matrix for Feature A and Feature B, which PRD §8 requires 'for both features'
cases.steps: Searched docs/implementation/invoice-due-dates-and-documents.md for a role × capability table.
cases.expected: PRD §8: 'The implementing session must produce a role × capability matrix covering ADMIN, CASHIER, VIEWER, CUSTOMER and the three POC roles for both features.'
cases.actual: The only such table is §4.5, lines 261-267, and its columns are 'View' and 'Manage' — documents only. Nothing states, per role, who may set a customer's payment terms, create an invoice, override a due date, read the ageing chart and with what coverage, filter by overdue, or export. Those answers exist but are scattered across §1 answer 2, §2.3 and §3, and none of them is expressed per role. The observed matrix for both features is recorded in data/role-matrix-observed.md.
